clue.text: Spring garment top lady discarded

indicators.note: discarded tells us the top lady is thrown out of the garment's letters

parts.note: a jumper is a knitted garment, a sweater
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the country's top lady

explanation.surface: A woman sheds the top half of her spring outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top lady discarded' takes ER, the Queen's royal cipher, out of JUMPER, the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to leap, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: 400-year-old material, account old boy's hidden away

indicators.note: hidden away means the account and old boy are tucked inside the material

parts.note: jean is a sturdy cotton fabric
OB, old boy, is a former pupil

explanation.surface: A four-century-old cloth with an old boy's account stashed inside.
explanation.walkthrough: '400-year-old' looks like wordplay, but it is the definition: the Jacobean period, under James I, began in 1603.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobean describes the reign of James I, 1603 to 1625, roughly four centuries ago.

clue.text: The old man's alert, nap having been disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of alert and nap are mixed

explanation.surface: Dad is wide awake after his snooze was interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old man' is slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternal means of or from a father, the possessive sense of father's.

clue.text: Repeated ceremony outside front of embassy highly thought of

indicators.note: outside says the ceremony's letters wrap around the following letter

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of embassy

parts.note: something highly thought of is well rated

explanation.surface: An embassy ceremony held outdoors that is much admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' wraps the ceremony round the first letter of 'embassy', and 'front of' picks that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean said or done again, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Get back, using transport outside city area

indicators.note: outside says the transport's letters go around the city area

parts.note: transport in the sense of ecstasy is rapture
EC is the London postcode district for the City

explanation.surface: Retrieving something by using a vehicle outside a district of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like vehicles but means delight; EC is the postcode of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapture something is to take it back, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Absurdity of cunning ruse, so, so misguided

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so these letters are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A sly trick that is so very misjudged it becomes ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: Incongruousness is being out of place or inappropriate, a close synonym for silliness.

clue.text: Popular novelist to steal from rubbish containers

parts.note: to rob is to steal
bins hold rubbish

explanation.surface: A bestselling writer pilfering from dustbins.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Robbins wrote huge-selling blockbuster novels such as The Carpetbaggers.

clue.text: Fighter in Carmen hurried, having met love briefly

parts.note: tore means rushed or hurried

indicators.note: briefly means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to adore is to love

explanation.surface: A character in the opera Carmen rushes off after meeting a brief romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' cuts ADORE to ADOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Escamillo in Bizet's Carmen is a bullfighter, the famous toreador of the Toreador Song.

clue.text: Bird landed finally on slope

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of landed

parts.note: a rake is a slope, as of a theatre stage

explanation.surface: A bird that has come down on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes D from 'landed'; RAKE is a stage's slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Sort of Egyptian policeman with stick bounds off

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman

indicators.note: with its bounds, the outer letters, taken off, stick leaves its middle letters

explanation.surface: An Egyptian police officer who has shaken off a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounds off' strips the outer letters of 'stick'; 'bounds' are its limits, not leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Copts are Egypt's native Christians, so Coptic describes one kind of Egyptian.

clue.text: Bishop to sin in famous wedding location in Aussie city

indicators.note: in places the bishop and the sinning inside the wedding location

parts.note: Cana in Galilee, where the Bible says water was turned into wine at a wedding
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A bishop tempted to stray at a celebrated Australian wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous wedding is the one at Cana in the Gospel of John, where water became wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is the Australian capital, so it is an example of a city in Australia.

clue.text: Remain cheerful as listener in inn being bowled over

indicators.note: in puts the listener inside the overturned inn
bowled over means knocked down and turned upside down, so the word for inn is written backwards

parts.note: a pub is an inn
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Staying upbeat while a listener in a pub is overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being bowled over' turns the inn upside down, giving BUP, and 'in' places the listener within.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear up is an idiom for coping bravely and staying in good spirits.

clue.text: Guide one vehicle around to face entrance

indicators.note: around tells us the vehicle is turned round, its letters backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Steering a single vehicle round so it faces the way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' turns the vehicle backwards to give NAV; 'to face' just sets the entrance alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide a craft or a route is to steer it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sign given by a queen, a king, and one leading American

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
I is the Roman numeral one
US stands for American, as in US goods

explanation.surface: A list of royal and American figures supplying a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' just shows I comes before US at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquarius, the water carrier, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Has man due to be disciplined to be repentant? No

indicators.note: disciplined means brought into order, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A man who has a punishment coming asks whether he should be sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without shame feels no remorse, the opposite of penitent.

clue.text: Nothing for securing a collar

indicators.note: securing means holding something in place, so the word for nothing holds the a inside it

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: No fastening at all for holding a shirt collar in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' looks like a shirt part, but it is a verb meaning arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to nail or collar a suspect both mean to catch and arrest them.

clue.text: Facility of some cafes in Bury, without any charge

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a net sum is what remains with no further charges deducted

explanation.surface: Free amenities at cafes in Bury, the Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the town near Manchester, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Internet cafes offer web access, so it is a service some cafes provide.

clue.text: Weep, having not finished work for harvest

indicators.note: not finished means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: to cry is to weep
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Crying over unfinished work at harvest time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having not finished' drops the final letter of the weeping word.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is the yield gathered from a field, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Money section's last bit in church newspaper

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: last bit picks the final letter of section

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: Cash from the end of a church newspaper section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last bit' picks the final letter of 'section'; 'church newspaper' looks like one publication but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Centimes are small coins, hundredths of a franc, so an example of cash.

clue.text: Criticise article about building in Rome

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it
the is the definite article
on means about, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: Slating a newspaper piece about Roman architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon is the domed ancient temple in Rome.

clue.text: Set off to see sweetheart maybe outside school

indicators.note: outside says the dating word goes around the school

parts.note: to date someone is to see a sweetheart romantically
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Heading off to meet a girlfriend away from school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' places the dating word around the school; Eton is England's best-known boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to explode it, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Wanderer has feet keeping less wet? The opposite!

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, here the dry word holds the feet
the opposite reverses the stated roles, so less wet keeps feet instead of feet keeping less wet

parts.note: drier means less wet

explanation.surface: A traveller with damp feet that ought to keep them dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, feet would keep 'less wet'; 'The opposite!' swaps the roles, so 'keeping' has the drier word hold the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is someone who roams aimlessly, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Phoney copies us, phoney looking good initially

indicators.note: phoney means fake, so the letters of copies us are falsely rearranged

explanation.surface: A fake that imitates us and seems good at first glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phoney' wants to be the definition, but the first one is the anagram signal; the definition is the second phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means superficially plausible but actually false, which fits a sham that seems sound at first.

clue.text: Please say nothing when given Polish drink

parts.note: sh is the request to be quiet
to rub is to polish

explanation.surface: Keep quiet when offered a Polish beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a cordial of fruit juice, sugar and spirit or vinegar.

clue.text: Dish youngster eats quietly behind house

indicators.note: eats means the youngster takes the quiet letter inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A child quietly eating a meal round the back of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: A hotpot is a British stew of meat topped with sliced potatoes, best known from Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotpot is a stew, so it is one kind of dish.

clue.text: Communication signal from character at back of group

indicators.note: at back of means the word for character comes after the group

parts.note: a ring is a group, as in a spy ring
tone is character or quality, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: A signal sent by someone at the back of a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone's ringtone is the sound announcing an incoming call.

clue.text: Male like Uriah Heep to talk indistinctly

parts.note: Dickens's Uriah Heep in David Copperfield calls himself 'umble, dropping his h

explanation.surface: A man as obsequious as Uriah Heep mutters his words.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep, the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield, keeps calling himself 'umble.
explanation.definitionFit: To mumble is to speak unclearly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sweet container taken around and held up

indicators.note: taken around tells us the sweet and container together are read backwards

parts.note: a sweet is a dessert, a pudding
a tub is a container

explanation.surface: A pudding pot carried round and then lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken around' reverses the whole of 'sweet container', so the dessert's letters end up last.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttressed means propped up or supported, as a wall is by a buttress.

clue.text: Native skirts round island, holy place

indicators.note: skirts round means to go around the edge, so the native's letters surround the island

parts.note: a son, as in a native son, is someone born in a place

explanation.surface: A local walking round an island to a sacred site.
explanation.definitionFit: Sion, or Zion, is the hill of Jerusalem and so a sacred place.
